name: Mount Hakusan (白山) by the Kanko Shindo, night at Murodo
why: One of Japan's three holy mountains: a ridge path through alpine meadows to the shrine lodge of Murodo, then sunrise on the 2,702 m summit with the priest.
book: Book Hakusan Murodo (open 1 May to 15 October, meals from July) by phone, 076-273-1001: no walk-ins. On peak days in July-October the road to Bettodeai is closed to private cars: park at Ichinose and take the shuttle bus (1,000 yen). Hokuriku Tetsudo buses run from Kanazawa on set summer days.
water: Springs at Kuroboko-iwa (Enmeisui); water, food and toilets at Murodo. Carry 2 litres for the climb.
dangers: Snow patches on the upper path until late June and early snow in October.
Thunderstorms on summer afternoons on the open ridge: be at Murodo by early afternoon.
Fog on the plateau: stay on the stone-paved path between Murodo and the summit.
turnaround: Not at Kuroboko-iwa by 14:00, or thunder: take the Sabo Shindo, the shorter way, or go back down to Bettodeai.

points.name: Bettodeai
points.note: 1,260 m: bus stop, toilets and the climbers' register. The Kanko Shindo climbs left of the suspension bridge of the Sabo Shindo, steeply up the Bettozaka ridge.

points.name: Kuroboko-iwa
points.note: A black volcanic rock at 2,320 m where the two trails meet, after the Tonogaike shelter and a meadow of summer flowers. Enmeisui spring just below.

points.name: Murodo hut, Hakusan
points.note: 2,450 m: four lodges for 750 people, a visitor centre and the Okumiya shrine at the foot of Gozengamine. Lights out at 20:30 in summer.

points.name: Gozengamine summit
points.note: 2,702 m, 40 minutes above Murodo on stones: the shrine priest leads a sunrise rite here in fine weather. The crater ponds lie just behind. Back down the same way.
